Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-4063", "title": "Carotid Artery Disease", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Your carotid arteries are two large blood vessels in your neck."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "They supply your brain and head with blood."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "If you have carotid artery disease, the arteries become narrow or blocked, usually because of atherosclerosis ."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Atherosclerosis is the buildup of plaque, which is made up of fat, cholesterol , calcium, and other substances found in the blood."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Carotid artery disease is serious because it can block the blood flow to your brain, causing a stroke ."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Too much plaque in the artery can cause a blockage."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "You can also have a blockage when a piece of plaque or a blood clot breaks off the wall of an artery."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "The plaque or clot can travel through the bloodstream and get stuck in one of your brain's smaller arteries."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Carotid artery disease often does not cause symptoms until the blockage or narrowing is severe."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "One sign may be a bruit (whooshing sound) that your doctor hears when listening to your artery with a stethoscope."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Another sign is a transient ischemic attack (TIA), a \"mini-stroke.\" A TIA is like a stroke, but it only lasts a few minutes, and the symptoms usually go away within an hour."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Imaging tests can confirm whether you have carotid artery disease."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Treatments may include: Healthy lifestyle changes Medicines Carotid endarterectomy, surgery to remove the plaque Angioplasty , a procedure to place a balloon and stent into the artery to open it and hold it open NIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1508", "title": "High Blood Pressure in Pregnancy", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "What is high blood pressure in pregnancy?"}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Blood pressure is the force of your blood pushing against the walls of your arteries."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Your arteries are blood vessels that carry blood from your heart to other parts of your body."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "High blood pressure , or hypertension, is blood pressure that is higher than normal."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Having high blood pressure can put you at risk for other health problems, such as heart disease , heart attack , and stroke ."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "During pregnancy, high blood pressure can cause problems for you and your baby."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "To keep you and your baby healthy, it's important to get treatment for high blood pressure before, during, and after pregnancy."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "What are the types of high blood pressure in pregnancy?"}, {"id": "S008", "text": "There are different types of high blood pressure in pregnancy: Gestational hypertension is high blood pressure that you develop while you are pregnant."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "It starts after you are 20 weeks pregnant."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "You usually don't have any other symptoms."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "In many cases, it does not harm you or your baby, and it goes away within 12 weeks after childbirth."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "But it does raise your risk of high blood pressure in the future."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "If it becomes severe, it can lead to a preterm birth or your baby having a low birth weight ."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Some women with gestational hypertension do go on to develop preeclampsia, a more serious type of high blood pressure in pregnancy."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Chronic hypertension is high blood pressure that starts before the 20th week of pregnancy or before you became pregnant."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Some people may have had it long before becoming pregnant but didn't know it until they got their blood pressure checked at their prenatal visit ."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Sometimes chronic hypertension can also lead to preeclampsia."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Preeclampsia is a sudden increase in blood pressure after the 20th week of pregnancy."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "It usually happens in the last trimester."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Preeclampsia also often includes signs of damage to some of your organs, such as your liver or kidneys."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "The signs may include protein in the urine (pee) and very high blood pressure."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Preeclampsia can be serious or even life-threatening for both you and your baby."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "If preeclampsia becomes severe enough to affect your brain function and causes seizures or a coma , it is called eclampsia ."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "In rare cases, preeclampsia symptoms may not start until after delivery."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "This is called postpartum preeclampsia ."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "If this type of preeclampsia becomes more severe and causes a seizure, it is known as postpartum eclampsia ."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "When a person with preeclampsia or eclampsia has damage to the liver and blood cells, it's called HELLP syndrome ."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Who is more likely to develop high blood pressure in pregnancy?"}, {"id": "S029", "text": "You are more likely to develop high blood pressure in pregnancy if you: Had chronic high blood pressure or chronic kidney disease before pregnancy Had high blood pressure or preeclampsia in a previous pregnancy Have obesity Are under age 20 or over age 40 Are pregnant with more than one baby Are African American Have a family history of high blood pressure in pregnancy Have certain health conditions, such as diabetes or lupus What are the symptoms of high blood pressure in pregnancy?"}, {"id": "S030", "text": "High blood pressure usually has no symptoms."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "People usually find out they have high blood pressure when their health care provider measures their blood pressure ."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Preeclampsia can cause other symptoms, including: Too much protein in your urine (called proteinuria)."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Swelling ( edema ) in your face and hands."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Your feet may also swell, but many women have swollen feet during pregnancy."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "So swollen feet by themselves may not be a sign of a problem."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Vision problems, including blurred vision or seeing spots."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Pain in your upper right abdomen (belly)."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "Eclampsia can also cause seizures, nausea and/or vomiting , and low urine output."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "If you go on to develop HELLP syndrome , you may also have bleeding or bruising easily, extreme fatigue , and liver failure."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "What problems can high blood pressure in pregnancy cause?"}, {"id": "S041", "text": "High blood pressure in pregnancy can lead to complications such as: Placental abruption, where the placenta (the organ that brings oxygen and nutrients to the baby) separates from the uterus (the place where a baby grows during pregnancy) Poor fetal growth, caused by a lack of nutrients and oxygen Preterm birth Your baby having a low birth weight Damage to your kidneys, liver, brain, and other organ and blood systems A higher risk of heart disease for you How is high blood pressure in pregnancy diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S042", "text": "Your provider will check your blood pressure and urine at each prenatal visit."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "If your blood pressure reading is high (140/90 or higher), especially after the 20th week of pregnancy, your provider will likely want to order some tests."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "These may include blood tests and other lab tests, such as a test to look for extra protein in your urine ."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "What are the treatments for high blood pressure in pregnancy?"}, {"id": "S046", "text": "If you have high blood pressure, you and your baby will be closely monitored to lower the chance of complications."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "You may need to: Check your blood pressure at home."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "Keep track of how many times you feel the baby kicking each day."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "Talk to your provider about what level of physical activity is right for you."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "Take medicine to control your blood pressure."}, {"id": "S051", "text": "Talk to your provider about which medicines are safe for your baby."}, {"id": "S052", "text": "Take aspirin in the second trimester, if you are at risk of preeclampsia and your provider recommends aspirin."}, {"id": "S053", "text": "Visit your provider more often to monitor your condition and your baby's growth rate and heart rate."}, {"id": "S054", "text": "If you have eclampsia , HELLP syndrome , or a severe case of preeclampsia , you will most likely need to go to the hospital."}, {"id": "S055", "text": "Your provider may also recommend delivering the baby early."}, {"id": "S056", "text": "They will make the decision based on: How severe the condition is The possible risks to you and your baby How far along the pregnancy is The goal is to lower the risks to you while giving your baby as much time as possible to mature before delivery."}, {"id": "S057", "text": "The symptoms of preeclampsia can last after delivery, but they usually go away within 6 weeks."}]}, {"id": "MLP-204", "title": "Hearing Disorders and Deafness", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "It's frustrating to be unable to hear well enough to enjoy talking with friends or family."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Hearing disorders make it hard, but not impossible, to hear."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Deafness can keep you from hearing sound at all."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Some possibilities are: Heredity Diseases such as ear infections and meningitis Trauma Certain medicines Long-term exposure to loud noise Aging There are two main types of hearing loss."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "One happens when your inner ear or auditory nerve is damaged."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "The other kind happens when sound waves cannot reach your inner ear."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Earwax buildup, fluid, or a punctured eardrum can cause it."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Treatment or surgery can often reverse this kind of hearing loss."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Untreated, hearing problems can get worse."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "If you have trouble hearing, you can get help."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Possible treatments include hearing aids , cochlear implants , special training, certain medicines, and surgery."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "NIH: National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1255", "title": "Yeast Infections", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Candida is the scientific name for yeast."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It is a fungus that lives almost everywhere, including in your body."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Usually, your immune system keeps yeast under control."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "If you are sick or taking antibiotics, it can multiply and cause an infection."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Yeast infections affect different parts of the body in different ways: Thrush is a yeast infection that causes white patches in your mouth Candida esophagitis is thrush that spreads to your esophagus, the tube that takes food from your mouth to your stomach."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "It can make it hard or painful to swallow."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Women can get vaginal yeast infections, causing vaginitis Yeast infections of the skin cause itching and rashes Yeast infections in your bloodstream can be life-threatening Antifungal medicines get rid of yeast infections in most people."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "If you have a weak immune system, treatment might be more difficult."}]}, {"id": "MLP-6236", "title": "Flu Shot", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "The flu (influenza) is a respiratory infection."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It is caused by influenza viruses that infect your nose, throat, and lungs."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "These viruses can spread from person to person."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Most people with the flu get better on their own, without medical care."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "But for some people, the flu is serious."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "It can cause complications and sometimes even death."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "People who are 65 and older, under age 5, pregnant, or have certain health conditions are at higher risk of flu complications."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Getting vaccinated against the flu each year is best way to lower your risk of the flu and its complications."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "What are the benefits of getting a flu shot?"}, {"id": "S009", "text": "There are many reasons to get a flu shot each year: It may keep you from getting sick with the flu."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "If you do get the flu, it may be less severe."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "You may also be less likely to have complications or need to be hospitalized with the flu."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "If you have certain chronic health conditions, getting a flu shot may help prevent the flu from making your condition worse."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "For example, if you have COPD or diabetes , the flu can worsen your condition so much that you might need to be hospitalized."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Getting the vaccine during pregnancy not only helps protect you from the flu during and after pregnancy."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "It also helps protect your baby from flu during their first few months of life."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "It has been shown to lower the risk of severe life-threatening flu in children."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "It may also protect the people around you, including those who are at higher risk of complications."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "The flu vaccine causes your immune system to make antibodies about two weeks after you get the shot."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "These antibodies provide protection against infection with the flu viruses that are in the vaccine."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "The U.S Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends annual flu shots for everyone 6 months and older, with a few rare exceptions."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Flu shots are especially important for people who are at high risk of developing serious complications from the flu."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "There are different types of flu vaccines."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "There are injectable vaccines (shots) and nasal spray vaccines."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "There are also some vaccines especially for people 65 and older."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Ask your health care provider which one is right for you."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "There are some people who should not get a flu shot: Children younger than 6 months of age."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Have severe, life-threatening allergies to flu vaccine or any ingredient in the vaccine."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "This might include gelatin, antibiotics, or other ingredients."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Some people need to talk to their provider before they get a flu shot."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "They include people who: Have an allergy to any of the ingredients in the vaccine."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Have ever had Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS)."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Some people with a history of GBS should not get a flu vaccine."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "If you are moderately or severely ill, you usually need to wait until you recover before getting a flu shot."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "You need to get a flu shot every year because: Your immune protection from the vaccine declines over time."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "You need to get the shot every year to boost that protection."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Flu viruses are constantly changing, so every year, the flu vaccine is updated."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "The flu vaccine will include protection against the viruses that will most likely be common during the upcoming flu season."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "For most people who need only one dose of the flu vaccine for the season, September and October are usually good times to get it."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "It's best to be vaccinated by the end of October."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "Some children need two doses of the flu vaccine."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "They should get their first dose as soon as the vaccine is available."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "They need to get the second dose at least four weeks after the first."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "If you are pregnant, talk to your provider about when to get the vaccine."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "When you should get it can vary, based on how far along you are in your pregnancy."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "Flu vaccines have been shown to be safe."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "But like any medical product, they can cause side effects."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "If you have any side effects, they are usually mild and go away on their own within a few days."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "Common side effects include: Soreness, redness, and/or swelling from the shot Headache Fever Nausea Muscle aches The flu shot, like other injections, can occasionally cause fainting ."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "In rare cases, some people have a serious allergic reaction ."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}]
